title: Run rule for a goto instruction
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, and let $ho$ be a register assignment, $p$ an input position, and $\ell,\ell'\in\Lambda$ labels. If the instruction at $\ell$ is to jump to $\ell'$, then for every output string $o$, the program reaches label $\ell'$ with registers $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$ within at most one step.
hypotheses_covered: The claim holds for every initial output string $o$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$ and $\ell$ a label whose
instruction is $\mathsf{goto}\ \ell'$.  Then for all registers $\rho$ and input
positions $p$, from label $\ell$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read the
program reaches label $\ell'$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read within
one step, without printing anything.
